overview: Two forms of endocytosis distinguished by what the cell is engulfing — solid particles versus fluid.
genZNote: Phagocytosis: cell eating solid food. Pinocytosis: cell sipping a drink.

aspects.label: Material Engulfed
aspects.valueA: Large solid particles, such as bacteria or cell debris.

aspects.label: Resulting Vesicle
aspects.valueA: Forms a phagosome, which fuses with a lysosome for digestion.

aspects.label: Cell Type
aspects.valueA: Performed by specialised cells like macrophages and neutrophils.
aspects.valueB: A more general, continuous process occurring in most cell types.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Both are forms of endocytosis and both are energy-requiring (ATP-dependent) processes, unlike simple/facilitated diffusion.
overlay.memoryTrick: Phago = eat solid. Pino = drink liquid.
overlay.commonMisconception: Pinocytosis is not selective the way receptor-mediated endocytosis is — it non-specifically takes in whatever fluid surrounds the cell.
